text: Question three. How do you evaluate a RAG system? Retrieval-augmented generation has two halves, so measure each one, and a failure points at its cause. Retrieval comes first, over a labeled set of queries and their relevant documents. Recall at k: did the right documents make the top k? And MRR, the mean reciprocal rank: how high did the first relevant one rank? Take three queries, each with one right document. The right one ranks first, third, and nowhere. Recall at five is two in three. MRR averages one, a third and zero: point four four. Then generation. Faithfulness: is every claim supported by the retrieved passages? Answer relevance: does it address the question? And citation accuracy. Faithfulness is judged against the passages, not against the truth. So a right answer the passages don't support still fails, because it's one you can't check. The follow-up: answers are wrong, and recall at five is point four five. Rewriting the prompt won't help, because more than half the time the right passage never reached the model. Fix retrieval first, with better chunking, hybrid keyword search, or a reranker. And don't just pass the top fifty instead. Models use the start and end of a long context better than the middle, so a few well-ranked passages often beat many loosely relevant ones. That's why a reranker earns its latency. Filing the ticket is where the assistant stops answering and starts acting.
